guard: A scope's failure record keeps a classified refusal's own code (#1519): a RuntimeFault the program caused settles under its catalog code with kind `runtime`, a plain non-EffectError throw stays the generic L4000 scope-fault, and a handler's own EffectError keeps its code and kind through recordableError. (FAIL-FAST suite: markers are upstream of the cells they guard.)
why: One settle site, three arms, and a mutation per arm: reverting the RuntimeFault arm to the flattening form is the exact pre-fix expression; disabling the EffectError arm flattens a coded handler failure and kills the preserved-code control; trusting any thrown object's `code` instead of the class check kills the L4000 control in the earliest scope-fault cell on the page.

mutations.name: the scope settle flattens a program's RuntimeFault back to the generic L4000
mutations.expectRed: a program refusal raised inside a scope settles under its own catalog code, not the generic L4000
mutations.completionMarker: the same rule on the scope's own failure record, which a fix at the effect site alone would leave open
mutations.cell: a program refusal raised inside a scope settles under its own catalog code, not the generic L4000
mutations.note: The exact pre-fix expression. With it back, the record says L4000 scope-fault with the L3021 sentence inside the message; the resume cell two checks later reads L4000 where the live run caught L3021, and this first red is the named assertion because the suite is fail-fast.

mutations.name: the EffectError arm is dropped and every handler failure flattens
mutations.find:
reason instanceof EffectError
        ? recordableError(reason, "scope-fault").error
        : reason instanceof RuntimeFault
mutations.expectRed: and a handler's own coded failure keeps its code and kind through the same settle
mutations.completionMarker: a handler's plain throw inside a scope still settles as the generic L4000 scope-fault, unchanged by the program-refusal rule
mutations.cell: and a handler's own coded failure keeps its code and kind through the same settle
mutations.note: The control that the fix did not eat the EffectError path: with the arm disabled, a coded L6002 handler failure records as L4000 scope-fault and the control goes red. The earlier unrecordable-detail cell stays green by coincidence (it asserts the same L4000 scope-fault the flatten produces), which is why this control names the code it must keep.

mutations.name: the class check is dropped and any thrown object's `code` field is trusted
mutations.replace: : { code: (reason as { code?: unknown })?.code as string ?? "L4000", kind: "runtime", message: messageOf(reason) };
mutations.expectRed: the scope wrapper is guarded too, on a real conclave, and the refusal is recorded against the scope
mutations.completionMarker: and it is blamed on the handler's dispatch, where L4000 already says exactly that, rather than on a code of its own
mutations.cell: the scope wrapper is guarded too, on a real conclave, and the refusal is recorded against the scope
mutations.note: The other direction of the fence: an unclassified throw now takes kind `runtime`, and the earliest existing scope-fault cell (the bind guard, whose NotCrossable reason carries no code) goes red on the kind. The new L4000 control further down reddens the same way; the first red is the named one.
